gap: No result ChatGPT got that I could read states that the three picks' cooling claims are three different kinds of number: ESR an average drop (6.5°F on its black listing, 7.2°F on its white listing of the same charger), Belkin a best case ("up to 12°F", internal test, smart fan on), and Anker no temperature figure at all on its US page.
standout_why: Compared against Macworld's ESR CryoBoost 3-in-1 review (cited), Macworld's UGREEN MagFlow Pro 3-in-1 review and Macworld's best-MagSafe roundup (cited). The ESR review repeats ESR's 6.5°F and 93.9°F figures but compares them with no other maker. The UGREEN review gives no temperature at all. The parts of the roundup I could load named only a Mophie 3-in-1 and a Belkin 2-in-1, with no cooling figures. Two cited pages could not be read: Digital Camera World's Anker Prime review returned only its headline, and techgearden.com failed on a certificate error. The other eight results were not opened. So the score is 2, not 3: the cross-maker comparison is new against what I read, and one half of it (ESR's 6.5°F) is already in a cited page.
decides: It confirms ESR as the pick on price but removes cooling as the reason. Belkin's 12°F cannot be read as nearly double ESR's 6.5°F, because one is a maximum and the other a mean, and Belkin's footnote names no ambient temperature or baseline. Anker's $229.99 'best premium cooling' pick rests on the hardware (thermoelectric cooler plus fan, TÜV label) and not on any published temperature drop. None of the maker claims I read supports ranking these three by how cool the phone stays; that would need a named reviewer's thermometer reading.
